title: Dar paso a: una realidad que sustituye a otra

sections.content: Dar paso a (to give way to) describes one situation, era, or system yielding to and being replaced by another -- a natural fit for narrating historical transitions. It's followed by a noun phrase naming what comes next. These sentences are taken directly from the previous reading.

items.spanish: La Unión Soviética dejó de existir, dando paso a quince nuevas repúblicas independientes.
items.english: The Soviet Union ceased to exist, giving way to fifteen new independent republics.

items.spanish: El sistema bipolar dio paso a lo que muchos analistas describieron como un nuevo "momento unipolar".
items.english: The bipolar system gave way to what many analysts described as a new "unipolar moment".

items.spanish: Esta interpretación daría paso más tarde a intensos debates académicos.
items.english: This interpretation would later give way to intense academic debates.

items.spanish: La vieja obsesión anticomunista cedería su lugar y daría paso a nuevas prioridades.
items.english: The old anti-communist obsession would step aside and give way to new priorities.

sections.content: Dar paso a describes a genuine replacement, not just a change alongside something -- the first thing effectively ends or steps back so the second can take its place, unlike combinarse con or sumarse a.
